title: Base change of a single normalized finite reduction
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite-dimensional extension E of Q_l, a morphism f : X → Y, and a positive quotient level n+1. Let aX and aY be natural identifications of finite constant set sheaves with the relative finite-label representables from [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]. Let q : O_E → O_E/(pi_E^(n+1)) be any continuous map of the corresponding profinite sets. Let rZ : pZ^* O_E → (O_E/(pi_E^(n+1)))_Z be maps of abelian sheaves, for Z=X,Y. Suppose that, for every profinite S and continuous g : S → O_E, the adjunction mate of rZ sends g, under aZ and the canonical constant/forgetful identification, to the relative scheme map Z[g followed by q]. Then f^*(rY), followed by the canonical finite constant-sheaf pullback identification, equals alpha_f followed by rX. Here pZ and alpha_f are [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] and [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp]. This statement concerns one finite quotient and arbitrary maps rZ; it asserts no integral isomorphism, ring compatibility or preservation of an infinite limit.

proof.text: The constant-sheaf pullback comparison preserves the sheafification unit: apply uniqueness of left adjoints to the constant/global-sections adjunction, and evaluate its global-sections comparison at the terminal object. The constant-ring/underlying-abelian-group comparisons also preserve this unit. Naturality of each finite-label representation for a singleton-to-label map identifies a constant label with its summand inclusion; the singleton relative test object is terminal because the test-object functor and scheme base change preserve finite limits.

proof.text: Compare the adjunction mate of the finite coefficient pullback isomorphism with base change of represented finite labels. They agree on constant labels by the preceding unit calculation and naturality of fibre-product associativity. The map from the constant presheaf into its sheafification is locally surjective, and the target represented presheaf is a sheaf. Separatedness therefore extends this equality to every section. This avoids constructing an inverse-image isomorphism for arbitrary representables.

proof.text: Use the existing unit_comp_lowerStar_map_unit_comp_upperStarComp identity for the morphisms to Spec Z. Evaluate at a profinite test object and use the component formula for the direct-image compositor: the mate of upperStarFromPointComp is the point-adjunction unit followed by restriction along fibre-product associativity. Take mates of the required equality under the composite point and f adjunctions. On each continuous section g, apply the finite-label equality from Step 2, the two assumed formulas, and naturality of the same fibre-product comparison for g followed by q. Injectivity of the finite representation and of the composite adjunction finishes. Empty profinite objects and empty schemes need no special cases.

theorem sfb_finite_reduction_pullback (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (n : ℕ)
    (aX : sfbFiniteConstantSets X ≅ sfbFiniteRepresentables X)
    (aY : sfbFiniteConstantSets Y ≅ sfbFiniteRepresentables Y)
    (q : sfbIntegralProfinite l E ⟶
      FintypeCat.toProfinite.obj (sfbIntegralFiniteLevel l E n))
    (rX : (coefficientRing X (sfbCondensedIntegers l E)).X ⟶
      (sheafCompose _ (forget₂ RingCat.{u + 1} Ab.{u + 1})).obj
        (integralCoefficientSheaf l E X n))
    (rY : (coefficientRing Y (sfbCondensedIntegers l E)).X ⟶
      (sheafCompose _ (forget₂ RingCat.{u + 1} Ab.{u + 1})).obj
        (integralCoefficientSheaf l E Y n))
    (hX : ∀ (S : Profinite.{u}) (g : S ⟶ sfbIntegralProfinite l E),
      (sfbIntegralFiniteRepresentation l E X aX n).hom.app
          (op ((profiniteToProEtOf X).obj S))
        (rX.hom.app (op ((profiniteToProEtOf X).obj S))
          (((sfbIntegralPointAdjunction X).unit.app (sfbCondensedIntegers l E).X).hom.app
            (op S) (ULift.up g.hom.hom))) =
        ULift.up ((profiniteToProEtOf X).map (g ≫ q)))
    (hY : ∀ (S : Profinite.{u}) (g : S ⟶ sfbIntegralProfinite l E),
      (sfbIntegralFiniteRepresentation l E Y aY n).hom.app
          (op ((profiniteToProEtOf Y).obj S))
        (rY.hom.app (op ((profiniteToProEtOf Y).obj S))
          (((sfbIntegralPointAdjunction Y).unit.app (sfbCondensedIntegers l E).X).hom.app
            (op S) (ULift.up g.hom.hom))) =
        ULift.up ((profiniteToProEtOf Y).map (g ≫ q))) :
    (f)^*[Ab.{u + 1}].map rY ≫ (sfbFiniteCoefficientPullbackIso l E f n).hom =
      ((upperStarFromPointComp f).app (sfbCondensedIntegers l E).X).hom ≫ rX
